questions: Did s-bend and slalom max_error fall below 0.0603 m (s-bend) and 0.0615 m (slalom), or did those runs progress further before going off track?
Did line_loss_events stay at 0 on all three tracks at 0.5 kg?
Did oval progress hold at or above 0.8, and did the oval finish count (10 of 20 at 0.6 kg) hold or rise?
Did oval steering_oscillation stay at or below 0.33 (0.316 at 0.6 kg)?
On the drift cases, does the controller now correct earlier at the edge, or does the robot still reach the 0.06 m edge at the same bend?
feedback_request.requested_changes_if_any: If oval progress falls below 0.5 or oscillation rises above 0.33, revert to mass 0.6 kg. If line losses appear on any track, revert to 0.6 kg as well. If s-bend or slalom still reach about 0.06 m with losses at 0, report which bend is the drift point so the next test can target it.

intent: Test whether mass 0.5 kg (lower yaw inertia than the 0.6 kg best) further reduces the edge drift on s-bend and slalom while line losses stay at 0 and oval progress holds near 0.9. Keep the 0.6 kg best as the revert point if oval progress falls below 0.5 or oscillation rises above 0.33.
learning: Iteration 8 showed that mass reduction from 0.8 to 0.6 kg raised oval progress from 0.71 to 0.89, halved the oval oscillation drift, and lowered the s-bend and slalom max_error slightly. Yaw inertia is therefore an effective lever that does not touch the sensors. The next test checks whether the trend continues at 0.5 kg, with the revert rule set at 0.6 kg because that is now the best measured mass.
rationale: Iteration 8 (mass 0.6 kg, otherwise iteration 5) is the best measured design at 257.45. Oval progress rose from 0.71 to 0.89 and 10 of 20 oval runs finished. Oval steering oscillation fell from 0.327 to 0.316, still under the 0.33 revert line. Slalom and s-bend line losses stayed at 0, and max_error dropped to 0.0603 m on s-bend and 0.0615 m on slalom, so the lighter mass helped the drift cases. The Integrator's rule for this outcome is to keep the lower mass and test the next step. I therefore set mass to 0.5 kg and change nothing else. Sensor layout (outer ±0.06 m, inner ±0.03 m, y 0.04 m), 12 mm footprints, 12 cm track, 3 cm wheel radius and body are all fixed, so any change comes from yaw inertia alone. Expected result: s-bend and slalom max_error below 0.060 m or further progress with losses still at 0, and oval progress holding at or above 0.8. The main risk is that oval oscillation crosses 0.33 as the robot gets lighter. Oscillation has been falling with mass so far, so I expect it to hold. If oval progress falls below 0.5 or oscillation rises above 0.33, revert to 0.6 kg, which is now the best measured mass; 0.8 kg is no longer the fallback. Iteration 7's inner ±0.04 m result and the rejected options in the Integrator's notes are not retried.
